subject: Mutual action: MAP + capacity runbook for Private/Dedicated lead times
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: John Sanders <john.sanders@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff: capacity runbook & lead-time assumptions for Private/Dedicated

John —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Per our call, I put together a short mutual action runbook focused specifically on capacity reservation timing and GPU-pool sizing options for the Private deployment you prefer. Key things to align on up front:

- Evaluation runway (POC cadence and acceptance criteria)
- Desired availability target (SLOs that drive pool size)
- Procurement windows and preferred commit cadence (single commit vs tranches)
- Lead times for Dedicated (hosted reserved pools) vs Private (VPC / on-prem appliance)

Attached is a draft MAP that pairs milestones with owners and realistic lead-time guardrails (aurelia_map_draft_v1.pdf). Quick summary of the capacity assumptions I used so we can validate:

- Baseline throughput target: 40 qps sustained (mixed short/long seqs)
- Initial GPU footprint recommended: 8 x A100-style cards (equivalent nodes) for stage 1 (PoC -> pilot)
- Ramp to production (x2) after acceptance: ~16 cards (split across 2 tranches if you prefer staggered procurement)
- Dedicated lead time (provisioning reserved pool in our cloud): ~6–10 weeks after signed commitment
- Private (on-prem/VPC) lead time including appliance + networking: ~12–18 weeks average; if air-gapped, add ~4 weeks for validation

Can you confirm your acceptance criteria for the POC (latency 95p < 300ms, stability 24h no OOM, sample eval scripts) and whether you want a single commit or tranches? Once we align, I’ll convert the draft MAP into a joint milestone table and circulate a version for procurement.

Next steps I’m proposing:
1) You confirm acceptance criteria and tranche preference by Thu 8/26
2) We lock the initial tranche sizing and window by EOD 8/27 so we can target Dedicated provisioning start week of 9/7 (if single commit)
3) Karthik will supply pricing/commit options and priyom will prepare the procurement checklist once we have tranche decision.

Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
- attachment: aurelia_map_draft_v1.pdf (MAP draft)
From: John Sanders <john.sanders@aureliahealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@aureliahealth.com
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: capacity runbook & lead-time assumptions for Private/Dedicated

Rafael —

Appreciate the concise runbook. A few clarifications from our side:

- Acceptance criteria: agree on 95p latency < 300ms for text generation and stability across 24h with a 2M token prefix cache test.
- For procurement speed we prefer a two-tranche approach: stage 1 (8 cards) to validate throughput, stage 2 (+8 cards) conditional on acceptance and budget signoff.
- Our security team needs the SOC2 + network segmentation checklist before we start private appliance procurement. Can you include the SOC2 artifact and a short matrix of network changes required?

If those items look ok, we can target stage 1 commit the week of 8/31 and aim for Dedicated provisioning start the week of 9/14 (we're in a tighter calendar for internal approvals).

John
John Sanders
VP Product, Aurelia Health
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: John Sanders <john.sanders@aureliahealth.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: capacity runbook & lead-time assumptions for Private/Dedicated

John / team —

Thanks — noted on the two-tranche preference. A couple of commercial / ops notes so we have alignment:

- Pricing options: 1) 12-month commit for tranche 1 (discount tier A), 2) staged commitment (6m + 6m) with lower upfront discount. I’ll attach a short price sheet once Rafael confirms the exact sku/bandwidth assumptions.
- Dedicated provisioning timeline: historically we hit provisioning start ~6 weeks after signed commitment + SSO/KMS onboarding. If Aurelia needs earlier starts, we can offer a short-term burst via hosted capacity while Dedicated is being stood up (this adds marginal unit cost but reduces time-to-PoC).
- For Private (VPC / on-prem) there are two tracks: appliance (Redwood-managed HW bundle) or customer-provided infra. Appliance track adds ~2–3 weeks lead time for shipping and 2 weeks for onsite validation; customer-provided runs on your procurement lead times (typical 10–14 weeks to get qualified nodes on-prem).

Action items:
- Rafael to publish an updated MAP with SOC2 artifacts and network matrix (Rafael)
- Karthik to push preliminary pricing & commit options (by Thu 8/27)
- Priyom to compile procurement checklist and DocuSign template (by Fri 8/28)

Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
- internal note: price_sheet_draft pending (will attach with sku list)

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: capacity runbook & lead-time assumptions for Private/Dedicated

John —

I’ve attached the updated MAP and a compact lead-time grid (redwood_private_leadtime_grid.csv) that maps our standard timelines to the paths we discussed. Highlights:

- If Aurelia signs a tranche-1 (8-card) commit by 8/31 we can target Dedicated pool provisioning to start 9/14 and be available for PoC testing by 10/2 (provisioning + validation + routing).
- If you choose Private appliance (Redwood-managed), earliest shipment after signed order is 9/21 with estimated onsite validation completed by 10/20. If you provide hardware, that path moves the critical path to your procurement lead time (we estimate 10–14 weeks typical).
- For the two-tranche plan I recommend this cadence: Tranche 1 (8 cards) — commit by 8/31; Tranche 2 (+8 cards) — optional commit by 10/15 with production activation target 11/1. This minimizes risk and spreads procurement approvals.

Attached files: aurelia_map_draft_v1.pdf, capacity_estimate_spreadsheet.xlsx, redwood_private_leadtime_grid.csv

Please confirm acceptance criteria and whether procurement will sign tranche 1 by 8/31. If you want, we can schedule a 30-min ops call tomorrow (8/28) to walk the lead-time grid with your security and procurement teams.

Rafael

Thanks for the clarity and the attachments — that grid is exactly what procurement needed. We ran the MAP by procurement and security this afternoon; two items:

1) Procurement verbally agreed to tranche 1 commit by 8/31, pending the final DocuSign. Please route the DocuSign to procurement@aureliahealth.com and cc me.
2) Security requested the SOC2 report and a network segmentation checklist. Laura — could you include a one-page soc2 summary and the network matrix on the ops call tomorrow?

We’ll take the ops call tomorrow 8/28 at 11:00am PT — invite accepted. Once DocuSign is out we’ll turn the signature process around quickly.

John
